To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conserved secondary structure elements of the bacterial ribosome proteins S20, 18 and 16, which contact rRNA, are present in the eubacterial ribosomal proteins S27A, S26 and 25.
the conserved secondary structural motifs of the bacterial proteins S20p, that contact rRNA, are found in the eukaroytic protein S25e.

structural motifs of the bacterial proteins S20p, which contact rRNA, are present in the eubacterial S25e, and that structural motifs of proteins S18p and of S16p are present in the archaeal S26e and eubacterial S27Ae proteins, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the eukaryal counterparts for the bacterial ribosomal protein families that are not present in the Archaea and Eukarya, which makes it possible to determine the evolutionary relationships between these ribosomal protein families.
the search for orthologues for the bacterial ribosomal protein families that have not been assigned in the eukarya and the identification of their structural motifs.
the identification of homologous families of the ribosomal proteins from bacteria and Eukarya.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all the 30S ribosome protein families of Bacteria, Eukarya and the Archaea are homologous.

the ribosomal protein families in the eukarya and archaea that correspond to the bacterial S6p family are not present in the bacterial S6 family, whereas those that correspond to the S20p family are present in the S20p and S20f families, those that correspond to S18p are present in the families S18p and L7/L12, and those that correspond to family S16p are present in families S16p, S16f and S16e
the bacterial ribosomal protein families, S20p, and S16p have orthologues, S25e, and S26e in eukaryotes, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of bacterial small ribosomal subunits are structurally similar to the eukaryotes and archaeal small subunits.
the bacterial ribosomal protein families are not homologous to those in Eukarya.
the bacterial ribosomal protein families, which make contact with rRNA in 30S ribosomes, are homologous, respectively, to the eukaryal ribosomal protein families.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structural motifs in bacterial ribosomal proteins that make multiple contacts with the 16S rRNA are preserved in the eukarya.
it is possible to predict the orthologues of bacterial ribosomal proteins by comparing the structural motifs of the proteins that make multiple contacts with RNA.
the eukaryal small ribosomal proteins S26 and S25 are the homologues of the bacterial S18 and S6 proteins, respectively, and that the eukariot S27 is the homolog of the bacterial S16.
